claim.value: Repeated elimination localizes the first revision associated with the defined tail-rate increase to the final boundary, conditional on valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition.
claim.scope: Conditional localization conclusion for the defined performance property.

contract_question: Given the cited premises, observations, and transferred mechanism, does the claimed target conclusion follow at the strength and scope stated?

target.title: Intermittent document export delays
target.frame: A hosted document service exports customer workspaces overnight. Median export time is stable, but roughly one in twenty exports now takes more than an hour instead of ten minutes. Export traces include queue entry, worker start, object reads and archive upload; trace coverage differs across worker versions. Customers cannot be asked to rerun large exports during business hours. The engineering team must plan a safe investigation and choose the next deployment action.

instrument.state: An ordered sequence of revisions contains a transition in a reproducibly testable property, with at least one earlier state known not to have the property and one later state known to have it.
instrument.operation: Test an intermediate revision, use the result to discard the incompatible portion of the remaining history, and repeat the partition-and-test process until the transition is localized.
instrument.signal: Each tested revision is classified on one side or the other of the target property, progressively shrinking the interval that can contain the transition.
instrument.inference: Repeated elimination constrains the first revision associated with the observed change to the final unresolved boundary or commit.
instrument.limit: Flaky tests, unbuildable revisions, nonmonotonic behavior, multiple independent changes, interactions among revisions, or an incorrectly chosen good or bad endpoint can prevent unique localization or identify a boundary that is correlated with rather than solely causal of the behavior.

P001.text: Act on the ordered deployment revisions spanning the suspected onset of unusually slow exports.

P002.text: The target property is an elevated probability of exceeding one hour under comparable workloads, rather than a change in median duration.

P003.text: The packet supplies neither a verified earlier good revision nor a reproducibly bad later revision; establishing these endpoints is a prerequisite.

P004.text: Before testing, define the reference workload mix, acceptable tail rate, material increase, confidence criteria and sample budget.

P005.text: Assume representative exports can be tested safely on isolated workers using authorized snapshots or scheduled overnight workloads; verify that assumption.

P006.text: Record worker revision, configuration, dependencies, workspace size, object count and concurrency so changes outside revision history are not silently attributed to code.

P023.text: Conditional on valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition, repeated elimination localizes the first revision associated with the defined tail-rate increase to the final boundary.

P028.text: Rare delays require enough trials: absence of a slow export in a small sample cannot establish goodness.

P029.text: Changing workspace mix, storage or network conditions, queue pressure, configuration and dependencies can confound revision comparisons; isolated replay may omit production interactions.

P030.text: Unequal trace coverage can create apparent phase differences.

P031.text: Flakiness, unbuildable revisions, several regressions, later fixes and interactions can invalidate binary elimination or leave several candidate boundaries.

P032.text: If results contradict a single transition, stop discarding halves and test smaller intervals or separate suspected factors.

P033.text: Report gaps and inconclusive endpoints explicitly.

P034.text: A localized boundary supports association under tested conditions; production causality and deployment safety require confirmation and monitored rollout.
